rows.description: A grandparent steps in with food, listening, and stability while my parents break apart. I feel safe but sometimes disloyal. Wise: accept the care with gratitude and keep including both parents.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, grief, guilt, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: I watch my brother or sister get gifts, trust, or praise I never get and feel invisible. Wise: tell a parent what I notice without attacking the sibling. Immature: making the sibling pay.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: favouritism, guilt, hatred, pride, resentment

rows.description: I keep a running tally of unfairness against my parent and stop confiding. Wise: raise it directly, using specific examples, and check whether I am also reading too much into small things.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, favouritism, guilt, hatred, pride

rows.description: I am the favourite and feel warm but uneasy, aware my sibling suffers. Wise: not to exploit it, to share credit, and to stay kind to my sibling. Harmful: enjoying the status or acting entitled.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, guilt, hatred, pride, resentment

rows.description: Being treated as the golden child, I feel guilty when my sibling is snubbed. Wise: gently include them and refuse to compete for the parent's approval. It is not my fault, but my behaviour matters.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, favouritism, hatred, pride, resentment

rows.description: My sibling hates me for being preferred and says cruel things. Wise: see the pain underneath, avoid retaliating, and ask parents to fix their behaviour. Harmful: rubbing it in.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, favouritism, guilt, pride, resentment

rows.description: I bond with the less favoured sibling against unfair treatment and we protect each other. Wise: lean on that closeness while staying respectful. Harmful: turning it into a permanent war against parents.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, favouritism, guilt, hatred, pride, resentment

rows.description: As the parent I favour the child who is like me and never notice the other shrinking. Wise: for a teen, understand this is usually blindness and not hatred, and tell them plainly what I need.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, favouritism, guilt, hatred, resentment

rows.description: We fight over the phone, room, and parental attention, each keeping score. Wise: agree on clear shared rules and ask a parent to referee once. Immature: tattling, hiding things, and escalating each round.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, dependence, envy, indebtedness, protectiveness

rows.description: I fight with my younger sibling yet turn fierce when outsiders tease them. Wise: this loyalty is real; show it more kindly at home too. Harmful: bossing them and calling it protection.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, dependence, envy, indebtedness, rivalry
